---
title: Restore archived contract data
description: Restore archived persistent contract data using the Stellar SDKs
---

<Info>

The manual operation (`RestoreFootprintOp`) is, for the most part, no longer needed starting in Protocol 23, as archived entries are automatically restored during `InvokeHostFunctionOp` when simulation includes them in the transaction's [restore list](/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/storage/state-archival#contract-data-automatic-restoration). `RestoreFootprintOp` can be used in rare use cases [described in this section](/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/storage/state-archival#restorefootprintop).

</Info>

This is a pretty likely occurrence: my piece of persistent data is archived because I haven't interacted with my contract in a while. How do I make it accessible again?

If you find that a piece of persistent data is archived, it can be restored using a Stellar transaction containing a `RestoreFootprintOp` operation. We'll make two assumptions for the sake of this guide:

- The contract instance itself is still live (i.e., others have been extending its TTL while you've been away).
- You don't know how your archived data is represented on the ledger.

The restoration process we'll use involves three discrete steps:

1. Simulate our transaction as we normally would.
2. If the simulation indicated it, we perform restoration with a `RestoreFootprintOp` operation using the hints we got from the simulation.
3. We retry running our initial transaction.

Here's a function called `submitOrRestoreAndRetry()` (`submit_or_restore_and_retry()` in Python) that will take care of all those steps for us. The Java version is a method to add to the `SubmitTx` class:

<Info>

This guide makes use of the (aptly named) `submitTx` function (`submit_tx` in Python) we created in [another guide](/docs/build/guides/transactions/submit-transaction-wait).

</Info>

<CodeGroup>

```typescript JavaScript
import {
  Networks,
  Keypair,
  Operation,
  TransactionBuilder,
  SorobanDataBuilder,
  rpc as StellarRpc,
  xdr,
} from "@stellar/stellar-sdk"; // add'l imports to submitTx
const { Api, assembleTransaction } = StellarRpc;

// assume that `server` is the Server() instance from the submitTx

async function submitOrRestoreAndRetry(
  signer: Keypair,
  tx: Transaction,
): Promise<Api.GetTransactionResponse> {
  // We can't use `prepareTransaction` here because we want to do
  // restoration if necessary, basically assembling the simulation ourselves.
  const sim = await server.simulateTransaction(tx);

  // Other failures are out of scope of this tutorial.
  if (!Api.isSimulationSuccess(sim)) {
    throw sim;
  }

  // No restorePreamble (the usual case since Protocol 23): just send it.
  // The invocation restores any archived entries in its restore list.
  if (!Api.isSimulationRestore(sim)) {
    const prepTx = assembleTransaction(tx, sim).build();
    prepTx.sign(signer);
    return submitTx(prepTx);
  }

  // Build the restoration operation using the RPC server's hints.
  const account = await server.getAccount(signer.publicKey());

  // Bid what recent transactions paid, capped at what you're willing to spend,
  // then add the resource fee from the restore preamble.
  const { sorobanInclusionFee } = await server.getFeeStats();
  const MAX_FEE = 100_000; // stroops per operation (0.01 XLM): pick your own cap
  let fee = Math.min(Number(sorobanInclusionFee.p90), MAX_FEE);
  fee += parseInt(sim.restorePreamble.minResourceFee);

  const restoreTx = new TransactionBuilder(account, { fee: fee.toString() })
    .setNetworkPassphrase(Networks.TESTNET)
    .setSorobanData(sim.restorePreamble.transactionData.build())
    .addOperation(Operation.restoreFootprint({}))
    .setTimeout(30)
    .build();

  restoreTx.sign(signer);

  const resp = await submitTx(restoreTx);
  if (resp.status !== Api.GetTransactionStatus.SUCCESS) {
    throw resp;
  }

  // now that we've restored the necessary data, we can retry our tx using
  // the initial data from the simulation (which, hopefully, is still
  // up-to-date)
  const retryTxBuilder = TransactionBuilder.cloneFrom(tx, {
    fee: (parseInt(tx.fee) + parseInt(sim.minResourceFee)).toString(),
    sorobanData: sim.transactionData.build(),
  });
  // because we consumed a sequence number when restoring, we need to make sure
  // we set the correct value on this copy
  retryTxBuilder.source.incrementSequenceNumber();

  const retryTx = retryTxBuilder.build();
  retryTx.sign(signer);

  return submitTx(retryTx);
}
```

```python Python
from stellar_sdk import Keypair, Network, TransactionBuilder, TransactionEnvelope
from stellar_sdk.soroban_rpc import GetTransactionResponse, GetTransactionStatus

# assume that `server` is the SorobanServer() instance from submit_tx


def submit_or_restore_and_retry(
    signer: Keypair, tx: TransactionEnvelope
) -> GetTransactionResponse:
    # We simulate first, instead of letting `prepare_transaction` do it,
    # because we want to do restoration if necessary.
    sim = server.simulate_transaction(tx)

    # Other failures are out of scope of this tutorial.
    if sim.error:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Simulation failed: {sim.error}")

    # No restore_preamble (the usual case since Protocol 23): just send it.
    # The invocation restores any archived entries in its restore list.
    if sim.restore_preamble is None:
        prep_tx = server.prepare_transaction(tx, sim)
        prep_tx.sign(signer)
        return submit_tx(prep_tx)

    # Build the restoration operation using the RPC server's hints.
    account = server.load_account(signer.public_key)

    # Bid what recent transactions paid, capped at what you're willing to spend,
    # then add the resource fee from the restore preamble.
    MAX_FEE = 100_000  # stroops per operation (0.01 XLM): pick your own cap
    fee = min(server.get_fee_stats().soroban_inclusion_fee.p90, MAX_FEE)
    fee += sim.restore_preamble.min_resource_fee

    restore_tx = (
        TransactionBuilder(
            source_account=account,
            network_passphrase=Network.TESTNET_NETWORK_PASSPHRASE,
            base_fee=fee,
        )
        .set_soroban_data(sim.restore_preamble.transaction_data)
        .append_restore_footprint_op()
        .set_timeout(30)
        .build()
    )

    restore_tx.sign(signer)

    resp = submit_tx(restore_tx)
    if resp.status != GetTransactionStatus.SUCCESS:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Restoration failed: {resp.status}")

    # now that we've restored the necessary data, we can retry our tx using
    # the initial data from the simulation (which, hopefully, is still
    # up-to-date)
    retry_tx = server.prepare_transaction(tx, sim)
    # because we consumed a sequence number when restoring, we need to make sure
    # we set the correct value on this copy
    retry_tx.transaction.sequence += 1
    retry_tx.sign(signer)

    return submit_tx(retry_tx)
```

```go Go
// Add these imports to the ones from submitTx:
//
//   "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/keypair"
//   "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/network"
//   "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/xdr"
//
// assume that `server` is the client from submitTx

func submitOrRestoreAndRetry(
  ctx context.Context,
  signer *keypair.Full,
  tx *txnbuild.Transaction,
) (protocol.GetTransactionResponse, error) {
  var none protocol.GetTransactionResponse

  // We simulate first and assemble the result ourselves, because we want to
  // do restoration if necessary.
  envelope, err := tx.Base64()
  if err != nil {
    return none, err
  }
  sim, err := server.SimulateTransaction(ctx, protocol.SimulateTransactionRequest{Transaction: envelope})
  if err != nil {
    return none, err
  }

  // Other failures are out of scope of this tutorial.
  if sim.Error != "" {
    return none, fmt.Errorf("simulation failed: %s", sim.Error)
  }

  // No RestorePreamble (the usual case since Protocol 23): just send it.
  // The invocation restores any archived entries in its restore list.
  if sim.RestorePreamble == nil {
    prepTx, err := assembleTransaction(tx, sim, tx.SequenceNumber())
    if err != nil {
      return none, err
    }
    prepTx, err = prepTx.Sign(network.TestNetworkPassphrase, signer)
    if err != nil {
      return none, err
    }
    return submitTx(ctx, prepTx.ToGenericTransaction())
  }

  // Build the restoration operation using the RPC server's hints.
  account, err := server.LoadAccount(ctx, signer.Address())
  if err != nil {
    return none, err
  }

  // Bid what recent transactions paid, capped at what you're willing to spend.
  // NewTransaction adds the resource fee from the restore preamble's
  // transaction data on top of this inclusion fee.
  feeStats, err := server.GetFeeStats(ctx)
  if err != nil {
    return none, err
  }
  const maxFee = 100_000 // stroops per operation (0.01 XLM): pick your own cap
  fee := min(int64(feeStats.SorobanInclusionFee.P90), maxFee)

  var restoreData xdr.SorobanTransactionData
  if err := xdr.SafeUnmarshalBase64(sim.RestorePreamble.TransactionDataXDR, &restoreData); err != nil {
    return none, err
  }
  restoreTx, err := txnbuild.NewTransaction(txnbuild.TransactionParams{
    SourceAccount:        account,
    IncrementSequenceNum: true,
    BaseFee:              fee,
    Preconditions:        txnbuild.Preconditions{TimeBounds: txnbuild.NewTimeout(30)},
    Operations: []txnbuild.Operation{
      &txnbuild.RestoreFootprint{
        Ext: xdr.TransactionExt{V: 1, SorobanData: &restoreData},
      },
    },
  })
  if err != nil {
    return none, err
  }

  restoreTx, err = restoreTx.Sign(network.TestNetworkPassphrase, signer)
  if err != nil {
    return none, err
  }

  if _, err := submitTx(ctx, restoreTx.ToGenericTransaction()); err != nil {
    return none, fmt.Errorf("restoration failed: %w", err)
  }

  // now that we've restored the necessary data, we can retry our tx using
  // the initial data from the simulation (which, hopefully, is still
  // up-to-date)
  // because we consumed a sequence number when restoring, we need to make sure
  // we set the correct value on this copy
  retryTx, err := assembleTransaction(tx, sim, tx.SequenceNumber()+1)
  if err != nil {
    return none, err
  }
  retryTx, err = retryTx.Sign(network.TestNetworkPassphrase, signer)
  if err != nil {
    return none, err
  }

  return submitTx(ctx, retryTx.ToGenericTransaction())
}

// assembleTransaction builds tx again at the given sequence number, with the
// simulated resources, resource fee, and authorization entries.
func assembleTransaction(
  tx *txnbuild.Transaction,
  sim protocol.SimulateTransactionResponse,
  sequence int64,
) (*txnbuild.Transaction, error) {
  var sorobanData xdr.SorobanTransactionData
  if err := xdr.SafeUnmarshalBase64(sim.TransactionDataXDR, &sorobanData); err != nil {
    return nil, err
  }
  original, ok := tx.Operations()[0].(*txnbuild.InvokeHostFunction)
  if !ok {
    return nil, errors.New("expected an InvokeHostFunction operation")
  }
  // Work on a copy, so that tx itself stays unchanged.
  operation := *original
  operation.Ext = xdr.TransactionExt{V: 1, SorobanData: &sorobanData}

  // Keep the operation's own auth entries; otherwise use the simulated ones.
  if len(operation.Auth) == 0 && len(sim.Results) > 0 && sim.Results[0].AuthXDR != nil {
    for _, entryXDR := range *sim.Results[0].AuthXDR {
      var entry xdr.SorobanAuthorizationEntry
      if err := xdr.SafeUnmarshalBase64(entryXDR, &entry); err != nil {
        return nil, err
      }
      operation.Auth = append(operation.Auth, entry)
    }
  }

  source := tx.SourceAccount()
  source.Sequence = sequence
  return txnbuild.NewTransaction(txnbuild.TransactionParams{
    SourceAccount: &source,
    BaseFee:       tx.BaseFee(),
    Memo:          tx.Memo(),
    Preconditions: txnbuild.Preconditions{TimeBounds: tx.Timebounds()},
    Operations:    []txnbuild.Operation{&operation},
  })
}
```

```java Java
// Add these imports to the ones from SubmitTx:
//
//   import org.stellar.sdk.Account;
//   import org.stellar.sdk.KeyPair;
//   import org.stellar.sdk.Network;
//   import org.stellar.sdk.TransactionBuilder;
//   import org.stellar.sdk.TransactionBuilderAccount;
//   import org.stellar.sdk.operations.RestoreFootprintOperation;
//   import org.stellar.sdk.responses.sorobanrpc.SimulateTransactionResponse;
//
// assume that `server` is the SorobanServer from SubmitTx

public static GetTransactionResponse submitOrRestoreAndRetry(KeyPair signer, Transaction tx)
    throws InterruptedException {
  // We simulate first, instead of letting `prepareTransaction` do it,
  // because we want to do restoration if necessary.
  SimulateTransactionResponse sim = server.simulateTransaction(tx);

  // Other failures are out of scope of this tutorial.
  if (sim.getError() != null) {
    throw new IllegalStateException("Simulation failed: " + sim.getError());
  }

  // No restorePreamble (the usual case since Protocol 23): just send it.
  // The invocation restores any archived entries in its restore list.
  if (sim.getRestorePreamble() == null) {
    Transaction prepTx = server.prepareTransaction(tx, sim);
    prepTx.sign(signer);
    return submitTx(prepTx);
  }

  // Build the restoration operation using the RPC server's hints.
  TransactionBuilderAccount account = server.getAccount(signer.getAccountId());

  // Bid what recent transactions paid, capped at what you're willing to spend,
  // then add the resource fee from the restore preamble.
  long maxFee = 100_000L; // stroops per operation (0.01 XLM): pick your own cap
  long fee = Math.min(server.getFeeStats().getSorobanInclusionFee().getP90(), maxFee);
  fee += sim.getRestorePreamble().getMinResourceFee();

  Transaction restoreTx = new TransactionBuilder(account, Network.TESTNET)
    .setBaseFee(fee)
    .setSorobanData(sim.getRestorePreamble().getTransactionData())
    .addOperation(RestoreFootprintOperation.builder().build())
    .setTimeout(30)
    .build();

  restoreTx.sign(signer);

  // submitTx throws if the restoration does not succeed
  submitTx(restoreTx);

  // now that we've restored the necessary data, we can retry our tx using
  // the initial data from the simulation (which, hopefully, is still
  // up-to-date)
  // because we consumed a sequence number when restoring, we need to make sure
  // we set the correct value on this copy: build() adds one to the sequence
  // number of `retrySource`, so the copy uses tx's sequence number plus one
  Account retrySource = new Account(tx.getSourceAccount(), tx.getSequenceNumber());
  Transaction retryBase = new TransactionBuilder(retrySource, tx.getNetwork())
    .setBaseFee(tx.getFee())
    .addOperation(tx.getOperations()[0])
    .addMemo(tx.getMemo())
    .addPreconditions(tx.getPreconditions())
    .build();
  Transaction retryTx = SorobanServer.assembleTransaction(retryBase, sim);
  retryTx.sign(signer);

  return submitTx(retryTx);
}
```
